suggestions.rationale: Depression is a common psychiatric comorbidity reported in myasthenia gravis, but prevalence evidence does not establish that MG caused or aggravated an individual's depressive disorder. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 38 studies estimated pooled depression prevalence at 36% among people with MG. Disease severity, fatigue, activities-of-daily-living burden, bulbar or respiratory symptoms, treatment exposure, sleep, disability, psychosocial factors, and prior psychiatric history require case-specific review.
evidenceGaps: Neurology documentation confirming myasthenia-gravis phenotype, severity, treatment, and functional burden
Depressive-disorder diagnosis, severity, and chronology relative to MG onset and changes in disease activity
Fatigue, sleep, bulbar or respiratory symptoms, activities-of-daily-living limitations, medication, and psychosocial contributors
History of depressive symptoms predating MG or another independent psychiatric disorder
Qualified clinician assessment distinguishing common MG/depression comorbidity from individual causation or aggravation

sourceReferences.citation: Nadali J, Ghavampour N, Beiranvand F, et al. Prevalence of depression and anxiety among myasthenia gravis (MG) patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Brain Behav. 2023;13(1):e2840. PMID 36495116
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review/meta-analysis of 38 studies estimated pooled depression prevalence at 36% among people with MG; supports association/comorbidity research, not individual causal attribution.
